archetype.name: Rebuilding (defense-last)
archetype.definition: A team at the bottom of the league at both ends with no group grading above a D, coming off its fourth straight losing season and currently playing more for evaluation than for the standings.

report.headline: Worst net rating in the league, and the one win is earned honestly
report.take:
Chicago is 1-8, last on the site's Teams tab and last in Net Rtg at -16. That record is not the product of bad breaks. W vs Pt Diff sits at 0 and the margin implies exactly one win, so the standings describe this team accurately. It is losing by 16.67 points a game, worst in the league, and three of the eight losses were within six points. The pace of 104, well above the league's 99.3, inflates the raw scores in both directions, so the ratings are the cleaner read: an ORtg of 108.4 (25th) and a DRtg of 124.4 (30th), 11 points worse than the league average.

The defense is the core problem, and it is structural rather than a shooting fluke. Opponents take 37.2% of their shots at the rim, the most in the league, and the Bulls rebound only 67.2% of opponents' misses (29th). Opponents also shoot 39.5% from three (29th), and the defense forces few turnovers (12.2 Opp TOV %, 27th). Point guards have feasted: 31.22 points a game, 6.42 above their own averages. One small positive sits inside all of that. When shots do reach the rim, opponents convert only 62.3% (8th), so the issue is containing the ball before it gets there, not the last line of defense. This was already a 22nd-ranked defense last season at 118.1, and it has gotten markedly worse.

The offense has a different story, and part of it is noise. The Bulls take threes at the 9th-highest rate but hit only 27.2%, last in the league and 7.5 points under the league's 34.7%. Across the five seasons in their history the team never shot below 35.6%, so some of that will come back. They also get to the line at the 4th-best FT Rate (35.7), a real foundation. The bigger worry is who is taking the shots. Caleb Wilson carries a team-high 26.7 USG % at a 50.7 TS %. Josh Giddey runs the offense (76 assists) at a 50.1 TS %. Norman Powell, the backcourt's most efficient high-volume scorer at 57.7 TS %, is listed out.

The direction from here is up, but only to bad, not to respectable. Shooting regression alone should turn some of the six-point losses into wins. The defensive profile, though, is the one that drove last season's 31-51, and it is more extreme now. The bright spot is Jalen Smith. He has the team's best On-Off at 17.4 and a 58.9 TS %, and he ranks 21st among 91 centers on his tab. Built around his minutes, this team should look like a 20-something-win club rather than the 9-win pace it is on.

strengths.title: Living at the free-throw line
strengths.body: A 35.7 FT Rate ranks 4th, 7 points above the league, by far the best mark in the Bulls' recent history. It keeps the offense from collapsing entirely while the threes aren't falling. It is a style trait more than a hot streak, so it should mostly hold.

strengths.title: Jalen Smith's minutes work
strengths.body: Smith is the one regular whose minutes clearly help. He posts a +17.4 On-Off and a 58.9 TS %, and he ranks 21st of 91 on the center tab. His near-even BPM on a team this bad says the lineup math with him on the floor is real. More of his minutes, and Zach Collins being out forces that, is the clearest lever available.

strengths.title: Ball security and rim contests
strengths.body: The Bulls are not beating themselves with giveaways: their 13.3 TOV % ranks 11th, slightly better than the league. Opponents also finish only 62.3% at the rim, 8th-best. Both suggest the effort is there in spots. The failures come earlier in possessions.

concerns.title: A defense that lets everything in
concerns.body: A DRtg of 124.4 ranks 30th, and the reasons stack up: the league's highest Opp Rim Rate (37.2), a 29th-ranked Opp 3P %, and the 29th-ranked DRB %, so opponents get both the shots they want and second chances. Opponents allowed the same 129.33 points a game in October and November. That consistency makes this look like the team's level rather than a slump. The three-point defense may loosen its grip somewhat, but the paint and glass issues are structural.

concerns.title: Volume threes, last-place accuracy
concerns.body: A 46.4 3PA Rate (9th) paired with 27.2% shooting (30th) is a recipe for empty possessions. It is the main reason a team that gets to the line and protects the ball still ranks 25th in ORtg. Last season this team shot 35.6%, so a good part of this should regress upward. Even so, a normal shooting year only lifts the offense to below average.

concerns.title: Shots going to the wrong places
concerns.body: Caleb Wilson uses 26.7% of possessions at a 50.7 TS %, and Giddey's 50.1 TS % comes with the ball in his hands. Powell, at 57.7 TS % on 25.4 USG %, is out. Meanwhile the efficient options, Smith and Tre Jones (59 TS %, the only positive BPM among the regulars at 1.7), are lower in the pecking order. Until the usage tilts toward efficiency, the offense will lag even if the threes start falling.

trend.note: A 1-5 October became 0-3 in November, part of a seven-game losing streak. The last five games ran 1.67 points a game better on margin than the season but still went 0-5. The defense has been identically bad in both months.

weekAhead.headline: Three top-13 teams plus a back-to-back ending in Minnesota
weekAhead.body:
There is no soft spot in this week. San Antonio (8-2, 5th on the site) and Atlanta (7-4, 13th) come to Chicago, then the Bulls play at Minnesota, the site's No. 1 team, the next night and finish at Cleveland. The Spurs and Wolves both pair top-four defenses with A+ backcourts, exactly the profile that punishes a Bulls defense already allowing 31.22 points a game to point guards. Minnesota's 3rd-ranked ORB % against Chicago's 29th-ranked DRB % is a particularly ugly fit on the second night of a back-to-back.

Atlanta is the realistic chance. The Hawks rank last in FT Rate, so they won't exploit the Bulls' fouling, while their defense allows the 25th-ranked Opp Rim FG % and the 28th-ranked Opp Rim Rate. That plays into Chicago's drive-and-draw game. The catch is that Atlanta forces turnovers at the 2nd-highest rate, testing the one thing the Bulls do reasonably well. Cleveland is a middling team on paper, but its A- frontcourt goes straight at the Bulls' weakest area, the glass.

keyMatchups.title: Caleb Wilson against Atlanta's power forwards
keyMatchups.body: The Hawks allow power forwards 9.07 PRA over their usual output, the most in the league. That makes this Wilson's best chance all week to turn his high usage into efficient production. If the Bulls are going to win a game, he probably has to carry it here.

keyMatchups.title: The glass against Minnesota
keyMatchups.body: Minnesota leads the league in RPG and ranks 3rd in ORB %, while the Bulls rebound only 67.2% of opponents' misses. On a back-to-back that gap tends to widen. Second-chance points could decide that game before shooting does.

keyMatchups.title: Spurs defense shuts the paint
keyMatchups.body: San Antonio owns the 4th-best DRtg and the 2nd-best Opp Rim FG %, and it holds power forwards to the fewest points in the league. That takes away Chicago's free-throw-and-drive route. It leaves the Bulls dependent on threes they are hitting at a league-worst rate.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the three-point percentage starts climbing toward the 35-36% range of past seasons, since that is the fastest path to snapping the losing streak.

restOfSeason.body:
Two things should improve on their own. The 27.2% three-point shooting is far below anything in this team's recent history, and a healthy Powell would restore its best efficient scorer. Those two together should lift the offense from 25th toward the low 20s, much like last season. The defense is the harder case. Allowing the most rim attempts in the league while losing the defensive glass is the same profile that sank last season, only worse, and nothing on the roster sheet points to a fix beyond leaning harder on Jalen Smith's minutes.

Expect a team that wins somewhere between 18 and 27 games and keeps a net rating in the mid-to-high negative single digits. That is better than the current 9-win pace but still among the league's bottom few. W vs Pt Diff is at 0, so there is no bad luck to give back. Any improvement has to come from actual play, mostly shooting.
swingFactors: Three-point shooting regressing toward past seasons
Any improvement in paint defense and defensive rebounding

confidence.note: Nine games is small, but both ratings are bottom-five and the margin and record agree.
